newsitem.title: UK: European physical aluminium slow, premiums tick up.
newsitem.headline: European physical aluminium slow, premiums tick up.

text.p: Business in physical aluminium has been slack in Europe recently as players wait for sliding prices to hit bottom but premiums in Rotterdam have bumped slightly higher, traders said.
"Very little business has been done recently for prompt metal, but we've done some first quarter business," one said.
Consumers and traders are holding back as LME three-month prices hit fresh 2-1/2 year lows.
"The price is relatively low over a three-year period, but people are lacking confidence and nervous about where the price is going next," another trader said.
"A lot of people have had it wrong in the prompt physicals area, they didn't expect it to go this low and stay there and they're now staying back unless they really need to," he said.
Modest stock building, however, has been seen.
"Physical demand is not any different, it's not worse but it's not any better," the trader said.
Another trader said Far East demand was healthy. "We don't seem to have too much trouble placing our material," he said.
Premiums for LME-grade Russian ingots in Rotterdam have risen, but traders gave a wide range from $15/$20 to $22/$27. This is up from about $10/$15 in mid-September.
"Premiums have been marked up a bit on the basis of traders not producers or consumers," a trader said.
Another said: "All the Rotterdam are a touch firmer because people don't ship to Rotterdam any more. There hasn't been a premium making it worth your while."
Little off-grade metal was available, but there was a bit of A6 around, with ingot premiums at level to $8, traders said.
Duty unpaid premiums were also firmer at $25/$35, but duty-paid were only slightly higher at $103/$110.
In the US, Midwest premiums have picked up after traders lent metal during the summer lull, but found themselves short and had to buy it back, a dealer said.
Premiums have risen to $4.00-$4.25 for very nearby up to November from $3.50 several weeks ago.
Far East Japanese premiums have been steady at $55/$60, with Korea another $5/$7 above the Japanese.
